notes: Matching: lowercase the reported name; an entry matches if it contains any 'match' string and no 'exclude' string. Same-name variants (RTX 5060 Ti/4060 Ti 16|8, 3080 12|10, 3060 12|8, 3050 8|6, 2060 12|6, RX 9060 XT 16|8) must be told apart by reported VRAM; Apple variants by GPU core count (gpu_cores). RTX 20 laptops without Max-Q report desktop names.

NVIDIA fp16_tflops = dense FP16 tensor with FP32 accumulate (PyTorch default). fp16acc_tflops = FP16 accumulate (e.g. ComfyUI --fast fp16_accumulation): 2x on GeForce, equal on RTX A-series/PRO Blackwell. fp8_tflops = dense FP8 with FP32 accumulate (what torch._scaled_mm uses); GeForce Ada/Blackwell run it at half their FP8-with-FP16-accumulate rate (whitepaper: 4090 330.3 vs 660.6). fp4_tflops = dense FP4 with FP32 accumulate, full rate (5090: 1676 = 8x fp16). int8_tops = dense INT8.

Whitepaper values: RTX Blackwell WP App. A-C (5090/5080/5070 Ti/5070 plus 4090/4080/4070 Ti/4070, 3090/3080/3070 Ti/3070), Ada WP (3090 Ti, 3080 Ti, 2080 Super, 2080 Ti FE), GA102 WP (A6000, 2080, 2070 Super), Turing WP (2080 Ti, 2080, 2070 reference clocks; FE about 5-6 % higher).

Derivations (stated per device in tflops_basis): NVIDIA 'AI TOPS' are sparse; RTX 50 = FP4 sparse -> fp16 = AI/16, fp8 = AI/8, int8 = AI/4, fp4 = AI/2; RTX 40 = FP8 sparse -> fp16 = AI/8, fp8 = AI/4, int8 = AI/2 (ratios from the whitepaper tables; matches SM x boost within 0.5 % on desktop cards). Non-whitepaper RTX 30/20 cards: SM x boost MHz x 512 (FP16/FP32acc) and x 2048 (INT8) per SM per clock, the rate every GeForce generation from Turing to Blackwell shares in the whitepapers.

Laptops: NVIDIA laptop AI TOPS for RTX 50 Laptop GPUs (except 5050) and the 4090 Laptop imply clocks above the listed max boost (5090 Laptop: ~2.7 GHz vs 2160 MHz). fp16_tflops_max_boost_calc = SM x max boost x 512 is 10-25 % lower; real throughput also depends on TGP. Use the lower value for speed estimates.

Pro cards: A6000/A4000 have full-rate FP32 accumulate (GA102 WP). RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell: server page lists FP4 4 / FP8 2 / FP16|BF16 1 PFLOPS (sparse) -> full-rate FP32 accumulate assumed for all editions (BF16 always accumulates in FP32); INT8 not published. RTX 6000/4000 Ada: only FP8 sparse published; the Ada WP lists the same-die L40 at half rate, so GeForce ratios are used (could be 2x if full rate). RTX 4000 Ada: product page 427.6 vs datasheet 327.6 TFLOPS FP8 sparse; 427.6 matches the boost clock.

Precision support by compute capability: Turing 7.5 has no BF16/FP8 (BF16 models need FP16 or FP32), Ampere 8.6 adds BF16, Ada 8.9 adds FP8, Blackwell 12.0 (RTX 50, RTX PRO Blackwell) adds FP4/NVFP4. Laptop compute capability follows the architecture (developer.nvidia.com/cuda-gpus lists desktop SKUs only).

AMD: dense FP16/FP8/INT8 matrix (WMMA) figures straight from amd.com spec pages (sparse figures ignored). RDNA 3: no FP8, INT8 = FP16 rate. RDNA 4: FP8 and INT8 at 2x FP16, plus 2:4 sparsity. RX 9060 XT 8 GB shares all compute specs with the 16 GB card (AMD lists one spec set); its 150 W TBP comes from AMD partner material via search, not fetched.

ROCm 10.1.0 matrix (page dated 2026-08-26, 'applies to Linux and Windows', Windows 11 25H2, Adrenalin 26.10.41.05): gfx1201 RX 9070 XT/9070 GRE/9070, AI PRO R9700(S)/R9600(D); gfx1200 RX 9060 XT (LP)/9060/9050; gfx1100 RX 7900 XTX/XT/GRE, PRO W7900/W7800; gfx1101 RX 7800 XT/7700 XT/7700, PRO W7700; gfx1102 RX 7600. RX 7600 XT is not named (same gfx1102). Linux: Ubuntu 26.04.1/24.04.5/22.04.5, RHEL 10.2/9.8.

AMD 'PyTorch on Windows' matrix (radeon-ryzen docs, ROCm 7.2.1 + PyTorch 2.9, Windows 11 only, 'entire ROCm stack not yet supported on Windows'): RX 9070, RX 9070 XT, AI PRO R9700, RX 9060 XT, RX 7900 XTX, PRO W7900 (+Dual Slot), RX 7700; FP8 only on RDNA 4.

Apple: fp16_tflops holds GPU FP32 vector TFLOPS (Wikipedia 'Apple silicon' table: cores x 128 x 2 x clock; M3+ clocks from third-party measurements); Apple GPUs run FP16 at the FP32 rate. M5/M5 Pro/M5 Max/M5 Ultra/M6 add a Neural Accelerator per GPU core; Apple publishes only multipliers (apple_ai_claim), so treat their figure as a floor for matrix work. laptop = null: the same chips ship in laptops and desktops.

Apple bandwidth uses Apple's figures where published (M5 Ultra '1.2 TB/s' = 1228.8 theoretical; M1 68.25 theoretical). M6 bandwidth depends on memory size (153 GB/s with 16 GB, 170 GB/s with 24/32 GB). M5 Ultra 64-core ships with 96 GB, 80-core with 256/512 GB (Apple configurator; Wikipedia also lists 96 GB for 80-core).
New since mid-2026: M5 Pro/Max (Mar 2026), M5 Ultra and M6 (Aug 2026; M6 MacBook Pro Oct 27 2026), RTX 5070 Laptop 12 GB (Apr 2026). No M6 Pro/Max yet.

Not released as of 2026-11-14: GeForce RTX 50 Super (reported indefinitely delayed over GDDR7 shortage; absent from NVIDIA's compare page). Reports in Oct 2026 say RTX 5090 production is winding down and NVIDIA's store dropped the 5080; both remain common.
Not catalogued: China-only RTX 5090 D / D v2 (excluded from the 5090 match), RX 9050, RX 9060 XT LP, RTX 4000 SFF Ada (70 W, excluded), Ryzen AI Max iGPUs (gfx1151, ROCm-supported).
